instructions: Rinse the rice in a sieve until the water runs mostly clear. Put it in a pot with 2 1/4 cups water, bring it to a boil over high heat, then cover, turn the heat to low and cook for 15 minutes. Leave it covered off the heat until the shrimp is ready.
Meanwhile, pat the shrimp dry and transfer it to a bowl. Toss with the salt and black pepper.
Juice the lime, which should be about 2 tbsp. In a small bowl, stir together the lime juice, fish sauce, sugar, cornstarch and 1/2 cup water until the sugar dissolves.

Peel the outer layers off the lemongrass and finely chop the bottom 4 inches of each stalk. Mince the garlic. Slice the scallions, keeping the whites and greens in separate piles. Seed and finely chop the Fresno chili. Chop 2 tbsp of the cilantro.

Heat a wok or large skillet over high heat until it's very hot. Add 2 tbsp of the oil, then half the shrimp in a single layer. Cook for 1 minute without stirring, until the underside is pink. Flip them and cook the other side for 1 minute, then transfer to a plate. Repeat with the rest of the shrimp.

Turn the heat to medium-high and add the last 1 tbsp oil, the lemongrass and the scallion whites. Stir for 40 seconds, until they smell fragrant. Add the garlic and Fresno chili and stir for 20 seconds.
Stir the sauce again, then pour it into the pan. Let it bubble for 30 to 45 seconds, until it thickens a little and turns glossy.
Return the shrimp and any juices to the pan. Toss for 1 minute, until the shrimp is curled, pink and cooked through.
Take the pan off the heat and stir in the scallion greens and the chopped cilantro.
Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
Slice the Thai chilies and put them in a small bowl on the table for the adults. Serve the shrimp over the rice.
method_notes: Only two published versions of this exact dish could be read, and neither shows a rating, so the lead is the best-read one. Astray Recipes (an old online collection) gives the pan method: shrimp stir-fried until they change color, then lemongrass, scallion and chili for a minute over high heat, with fish sauce and a little cornflour-thickened liquid. Kingfoodmart (a Vietnamese grocer's recipe page) gives the sauce balance of fish sauce, sugar and lime juice, with garlic fried in with the lemongrass. Both are small-batch with loose amounts, so the quantities here are scaled up to 1 1/2 lbs by the sauce ratios. Shrimp is peeled for a family table. The base is mild: a seeded Fresno chili goes in the pan and Thai chili is served on the side. Fish sauce brands vary, so check the label for gluten.
